rows.name: STUB_MODE
rows.read_by: Stub `rinzler_proxy` program that the test writes (`t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py`)
rows.values: One mode name, compared as exact text: `ready`, `early-exit`, `never-ready`, `garbage-port`, `accept-then-close`, `garbage-http`, `big-body`, `die-after-publish`, `wrong-status`, `ignore-sigterm`, `term-exit-3`, `gap`, `slow-ready`.
rows.default: Unset: `ready`. A name that is not in the list also behaves like `ready`.
rows.effect: Selects how the stub behaves. For example, it exits before it is ready, or it ignores `SIGTERM`.
rows.notes: The launcher under test (`t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py`) copies its own environment to the stub.

rows.name: STUB_RUN_FILE_DIR
rows.read_by: Stub `rinzler_proxy` program that the test writes (`t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py`)
rows.values: Path of a directory.
rows.default: Unset: the stub creates no run marker file.
rows.effect: The stub creates the run marker file `rinzler-<pid>.run` in this directory when it starts.
rows.notes: The test sets a temporary directory. The tests check that the launcher under test (`t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py`) removes the file when it stops the stub.

rows.name: TEST_RUNNER_RC
rows.read_by: Fake runner program that the test writes (`bin/slice-tests/test_dice_lsf.py`)
rows.values: Integer text. The fake runner parses it with `int`.
rows.default: Unset: the fake runner runs the payload command of the job.
rows.effect: The fake runner does not run the payload command. It exits with this status.
rows.notes: No process reads it from its environment. The test passes `--env TEST_RUNNER_RC=7` to `bin/dice-lsf-submit`. That program stores the pair in the `env` map of the job envelope (the JSON file that describes one LSF job). The fake runner reads it there.

rows.name: TRON_BOOK_MB
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. One Slice unit test passes it to the Python function `make_test_env` of `bin/slice`.
rows.values: The test uses the text `512`.
rows.effect: Sample name. The test checks that `make_test_env` keeps a test-defined entry in the environment that it builds.
rows.notes: No process receives it. The test only reads the returned dictionary. The name is not one of the scheduler variables `TRON_BOOK_INITIAL_TOKENS`, `TRON_BOOK_MAX_TOKENS` and `TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR`.

rows.name: TRON_EXPECTED_NIXFMT_PATH
rows.values: Nix store path of the `nixfmt` package. The test compares it as exact text with each whole line of a file.
rows.default: Unset: the test fails with `Expected upstream nixfmt path is missing` when `TRON_REQUIRE_CLOSURE_AUDIT` is `1`. Otherwise the test does not read it.
rows.effect: The test searches the file that `TRON_LINT_CLOSURE_PATHS` names for a line equal to this path. When no line matches, the test fails with `Lint shell does not use nixfmt from the upstream package set`.
rows.notes: `flake.nix` sets it to the `nixfmt` package in the Nix check `lint-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs this test).

rows.name: TRON_GCP_NIX_PURE_CONTRACTS
rows.values: Only the exact text `1` turns the skip on. Any other text behaves like unset.
rows.default: Unset: all tests of the two files run.
rows.effect: With `1`, the tests that need a working Nix installation are skipped. These are 5 tests in `test_cache.py` and the whole class `GcpNixSourceInvalidationTests`.
rows.notes: Each file reads it once, when Python imports the test module. `flake.nix` sets `1` in the Nix check `ci-machinery-contracts` (a Nix build that runs these tests).

rows.name: TRON_GOLDEN_EXPECT
rows.values: Any text. The test searches for it inside the message content of the response.
rows.default: Unset: the test case skips this one check. Its other checks still run.
rows.effect: The test case `rinzler_proxy decodes golden tokens over HTTP` checks that the message content of the HTTP response contains this text.
rows.notes: An empty value always passes the check. The test case skips before it reads this variable when no model or no token ids are available. `TRON_TOKENIZER_PATH` and `TRON_GOLDEN_IDS` give them.

rows.name: TRON_GOLDEN_IDS
rows.values: Integer token ids separated by commas, for example `9707,1879,128009`. Each item is parsed with `std::stoi`. An item without a leading number throws an exception.
rows.default: Unset: the list of token ids is empty. Then 5 test cases skip.
rows.effect: Gives the token ids that `rinzler_proxy` replays as the model output. The test cases write them to a temporary JSON file for `rinzler_proxy`.
rows.notes: The test reads it only when `TRON_TOKENIZER_PATH` is set. One test case needs at least 2 ids. A comment in the test says that the list must end with the end-of-sequence id of the served model.

evidence.quote: if (model->golden_ids.empty()) SKIP("set TRON_GOLDEN_IDS for the decode assertion");
std::ofstream(golden_path) << ids.dump();  // bare array == default script

rows.name: TRON_LINT_CLOSURE_PATHS
rows.values: Path of a text file with one Nix store path on each line.
rows.default: Unset: the test fails with `Recursive lint closure manifest is missing` when `TRON_REQUIRE_CLOSURE_AUDIT` is `1`. Otherwise the test does not read it.
rows.effect: The test reads the list of store paths in this file. It fails when the list lacks the path in `TRON_EXPECTED_NIXFMT_PATH`. It also fails when the list holds the path in `TRON_SOURCE_STORE_PATH`, a first-party package or a `lefthook` package.
rows.notes: A first-party package has `tron`, `runtron`, `rinzler`, `tokenize_py`, `tokenize-py` or `positron` as a whole part of its name, with `-` as the separator. `flake.nix` sets the variable in the Nix check `lint-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs this test).

rows.name: TRON_LINT_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_PATHS
rows.values: Path of a text file with one Nix store path on each line.
rows.default: Unset: the test fails with `Recursive lint runtime closure manifest is missing` when `TRON_REQUIRE_CLOSURE_AUDIT` is `1`. Otherwise the test does not read it.
rows.effect: The test searches this file for a store path whose name has `-ghc-` or `-cabal-install-` before a digit. On a match the test fails with `Lint runtime includes GHC, its documentation, or Cabal`.
rows.notes: `flake.nix` sets it in the Nix check `lint-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs this test).

evidence.quote: fail 'Lint runtime includes GHC, its documentation, or Cabal'

rows.name: TRON_NIX_LEFTHOOK
rows.values: Absolute path of an existing file. The test expects the wrapper script of Lefthook (the program that runs the Git pre-commit checks).
rows.default: Unset: the test class stops in `setUpClass` with `KeyError`. None of its tests runs.
rows.effect: Names the Lefthook wrapper under test. The test passes the path to `bin/install-nix-hooks.py --lefthook`. One test case also runs `<path> install`.
rows.notes: A relative path or a missing file raises `RuntimeError`. `flake.nix` sets it in the lint dev shell that `nix develop .#lint` starts.

evidence.quote: if not cls.lefthook.is_absolute() or not cls.lefthook.is_file():

rows.name: TRON_POISON_BITS
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `std::stoul` and base 0: decimal, `0x` hexadecimal or `0` octal. The test keeps the low 16 bits. Text without a leading number throws an exception.
rows.default: Unset: `0`. The test writes zeros into the KV cache region of the HBM (the memory on each FPGA card). Empty: `std::stoul` throws an exception.
rows.effect: A value other than `0` makes the test write this 16-bit pattern over the weight region of the HBM of every FPGA card.
rows.notes: Both modes overwrite memory on every FPGA card that the test opens. CTest (the CMake test runner) does not run `t_clearhbm`. `t/CMakeLists.txt` registers it with `DISABLED TRUE`. `TRON_VERIFY_ECC` adds a check after the write.

evidence.quote: add_catch_test(NAME t_clearhbm LIBRARIES tron pos perfetto PROPERTIES RESOURCE_LOCK fpga LABELS fpga DISABLED TRUE)

rows.name: TRON_PROXY_WEIGHTS_ROOT
rows.values: Path of a directory.
rows.effect: Replaces the weights directory that `run_suite.sh` checks before it starts pytest. In every mode except `lib`, the script exits with status 1 when the directory is missing. A value that differs from the default makes the script print a warning in every mode.
rows.notes: It changes this check only. The Python test code (`t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py`) does not read it and keeps the fixed root `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface`. In the repository only `t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py` sets it.

rows.name: TRON_REQUIRE_CLOSURE_AUDIT
rows.values: Only the exact text `1` turns the audit on. Any other text behaves like unset.
rows.default: Unset: the test skips the closure audit and the `make lint-notes` check. Its tool path and version checks still run.
rows.effect: With `1`, the test runs the closure audit (a check of the Nix store paths that the lint tools depend on). It also fails when `ghc` or `cabal` is on `PATH`, and it runs `make lint-notes` on a sample file.
rows.notes: With `1`, the test needs `TRON_LINT_CLOSURE_PATHS`, `TRON_EXPECTED_NIXFMT_PATH` and `TRON_LINT_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_PATHS`. `TRON_SOURCE_STORE_PATH` is optional. `flake.nix` sets `1` in the Nix check `lint-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs this test).

evidence.quote: make lint-notes HEADERS= TEST_HEADERS= SOURCES= DOCS="${note_fixture}" \

rows.name: TRON_SOURCE_ROOT
rows.values: Path of a directory that holds TRON source files.
rows.default: Unset: each test uses the checkout that holds the test file. Empty: the shell test does the same. The Python test uses the current directory.
rows.effect: Selects the source tree that the two Rust toolchain tests use. The shell test reads `rust-toolchain.toml`, build files and `rust/` scripts from it. The Python test runs `rust/run-cargo-test-binary` from it.
rows.notes: `flake.nix` sets it in the Nix check `rust-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs both tests). The shell test gets the flake source. The Python test gets a temporary directory with copies of `rust/run-cargo` and `rust/run-cargo-test-binary`.

rows.name: TRON_SOURCE_STORE_PATH
rows.values: Nix store path of the repository source. The test compares it as exact text with each whole line of a file.
rows.default: Unset: the test does not look for a source path in the list. The test reads it only when `TRON_REQUIRE_CLOSURE_AUDIT` is `1`.
rows.effect: The test fails with `Public lint closure contains repository source path` when a line of the file that `TRON_LINT_CLOSURE_PATHS` names equals this path.
rows.notes: `flake.nix` sets it to `self.outPath` (the store path of the flake source) in the Nix check `lint-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs this test).

rows.name: TRON_TEST_NIX_OUTPUT
rows.read_by: Fake `nix` command that the test writes (`bin/ci/test_lint_diagnostics.py`)
rows.values: Path of a text file.
rows.effect: The fake `nix` command prints the content of this file.
rows.notes: The test runs `bin/ci/run-lint-checks.sh` with the fake `nix` command first on `PATH`.

rows.name: TRON_TEST_NIX_STATUS
rows.read_by: Fake `nix` command and fake `nix` shell function that the tests write (`bin/ci/test_lint_diagnostics.py`, `bin/ci/test_build_test_stage.py`)
rows.values: Integer exit status as text.
rows.effect: The fake `nix` command or shell function ends with this exit status.
rows.notes: Two tests set it. `bin/ci/test_build_test_stage.py` sets `0` and `23`.

rows.name: TRON_TOKENIZER_PATH
rows.values: A model name, for example `shuyuej/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GPTQ`. It is not a file path. `rinzler_proxy` puts `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/` before the name.
rows.default: Unset: the test uses `shuyuej/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GPTQ` when that model is installed. Otherwise 9 test cases skip. Empty: the test starts `rinzler_proxy` without `--model-path`.
rows.effect: Selects the model that the 9 HTTP test cases of `t_rinzler_proxy` serve. The test starts `rinzler_proxy` with `--model-path <name>:default:<name>`. Each request names this model.
rows.notes: When it is set, the token ids come from `TRON_GOLDEN_IDS` only. The fallback model counts as installed when `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/shuyuej/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-GPTQ` exists. The fallback uses the token ids `9707,1879,128009`.

rows.name: TRON_VERIFY_ECC
rows.values: Any value turns it on, also an empty value. The test does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: the test has no verify phase.
rows.effect: After the write phase, the test runs one matrix multiply on each FPGA card. It fails when a result differs from the value that it computes from `TRON_POISON_BITS`.
rows.notes: A comment in the test says that the verify phase is meaningful only after a write with a `TRON_POISON_BITS` value other than `0`. CTest (the CMake test runner) does not run `t_clearhbm`.

rows.name: UNRELATED_VAR
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. The test sets it for a run of `slice submit`.
rows.values: The test uses the text `kept`.
rows.effect: Sample name. The test checks that `slice submit` sends an unrelated caller variable to the Dice daemon.

rows.name: WINNER_TARGET
rows.values: Path of a file.
rows.default: Unset: the stub stops with the bash error `parameter null or not set`.
rows.effect: The stub creates a symbolic link from its last argument to this file and exits with status 1.
rows.notes: The stub runs the real `ln` named by `REAL_LN`. The test runs `bin/ci/ci-shared-nfs.sh mark-once` with the stub first on `PATH`. The test expects the helper to fail and to report the symbolic link.

new_terms.definition: A short program that a test writes and starts in place of a real program, for example a stub `ln` or a fake `nix`.
A test that runs as a Nix build. `flake.nix` defines it under `checks`. Example: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.lint-toolchain`.
The path of one package below `/nix/store`.
The part of `bin/ci/test-nix-lint-toolchain.sh` that checks the list of all Nix store paths that the lint tools depend on.
The program that runs the Git pre-commit checks that `lefthook.yml` lists.
The memory on an FPGA card. One region holds the KV cache and one region holds the model weights.
The JSON file that `bin/dice-lsf-submit` writes for one LSF job. It holds the payload command, the working directory and an `env` map.
The file `rinzler-<pid>.run` that rinzler creates when it starts.
The CMake test runner. `t/CMakeLists.txt` registers the tests that it runs.

notes: 22 rows, none dropped. 14 rows are hand_set true and 8 rows are fixtures. TRON_BOOK_MB stays as a fixture row: it is sample text that one Slice unit test passes to make_test_env, no process receives it and nothing reads it. Drop it if sample names that never reach a process environment are out of scope. TEST_RUNNER_RC is read from the env map of the LSF job envelope and not from a process environment. The row says so. TRON_PROXY_WEIGHTS_ROOT is hand_set true: the checked-in launcher t/proxy/run_suite.sh reads it, so a value in the environment of a person changes real runs. In the repository only t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py sets it, and the source calls it a test-only setting. The eight variables that flake.nix sets for a Nix check or the lint dev shell are hand_set true in group tool-tests. TRON_TOKENIZER_PATH is in group proxy with TRON_GOLDEN_IDS and TRON_GOLDEN_EXPECT: only t_rinzler_proxy reads the three, and the value is a model name, not a path. TRON_TEST_NIX_STATUS has 2 setter files. set_in names 1 file and the notes cell names the other. TRON_SOURCE_ROOT and TRON_TOKENIZER_PATH and TRON_POISON_BITS carry an Empty clause: an empty value behaves differently from unset. All evidence quotes are the whole source line without indentation, except bin/ci/test-nix-lint-toolchain.sh:152. That quote is an exact part of the line. The rest of the line holds a vertical bar inside a regular expression. Failure messages that sit on source lines with the shell operator made of 2 vertical bars are not quoted. The quoted neighbour lines are 1 or 2 lines above them. The example value of TRON_GOLDEN_IDS is the fallback id list in t/t_rinzler_proxy.cpp, not the README.proxy.md example.
